T1.evidence: chat_code_flags=0 and no fenced implementation/test code appears in any tutor turn; tutor uses prose sketches, pseudocode option names ('A'/'B'), and line references only (e.g. turn 19's A/B choice described in prose).

T2.evidence: Tutor repeatedly caught learner's false progress claims against real referee output: turn 7 corrected 'AssertionError' to actual ERROR, turn 14 caught false DONE with pasted real traceback ('AttributeError: tuple object has no attribute type'), and turn 21 corrected a misremembered failure cause with the actual traceback.

T3.evidence: Mostly single, targeted Socratic questions each turn (e.g. turn 17's hand-trace question); occasional two-part compound questions (turn 14: 'what would produce this... and why did you say DONE') and turn 25 stacks two questions, slightly below ideal single-question rung climbing.

T4.evidence: Steady forward motion turn over turn (errors dropped 7→5→2→1→0 across turns 17-27) with stuckness on the whitelist/EOF bug resolved within about 2-3 rungs (turns 18-20's A/B narrowing).

T5.evidence: Tutor named the false DONE claim explicitly at turn 14 ('you reported DONE without this being true') and again flagged a second fabricated-output describe-from-memory pattern at turn 21 ('third time now you've described an error from memory'), converting both into a verification-habit lesson.

S1.evidence: Final calc.py is a clean, idiomatic recursive-descent parser with namedtuple tokens and simplified boundary checks after redundant whitelists were removed (turn 27-28); minor rough edge is the mutable dict-based position tracker instead of a class/nonlocal, a stylistic nit not a defect.

S2.evidence: Learner correctly traced tokens by hand (turn 18: 'lex returns two tokens... state[position] is 1 but len(tokens) is 2') and reasoned through the EOF/RPAREN redundancy at turn 27, though two turns (17, 21) show mistaken guesses about causes before verifying against real output.

S3.evidence: One fabricated DONE claim at turn 14 caught by the tutor, plus repeated pattern of describing errors from memory rather than pasted output (flagged again at turn 21); each was corrected and not repeated after turn 21's warning, but the repetition itself keeps this below a clean 4-5.

S4.evidence: Learner proposed next steps unprompted multiple times (e.g. turn 12 proposing full test suite, turn 22 diagnosing the NEGATIVE/MINUS token issue) and self-corrected direction once nudged, needing only pointers rather than being dragged through each step.

overall_note: A well-grounded, TDD-anchored tutoring session with zero code leakage and strong integrity handling of two false-claim incidents, though the learner's habit of guessing at output before verifying and one false DONE keep S3 at baseline rather than exemplary.
